claims.quote: It startled me to read the passage in which Edith shows the musical schedule to Julian West, and tells him to choose which selection he wishes to have brought through the air into the music room.
claims.description: The introduction notes that the novel foresaw on-demand music piped into homes from a published schedule, like radio broadcasting.

claims.quote: showed how, by turning a screw, the volume of the music could be made to fill the room, or die away to an echo so faint and far that one could scarcely be sure whether he heard or imagined it.
claims.description: The introduction quotes the novel's home music receiver with an adjustable volume control.

claims.quote: the possibility of hearing a sermon without going to church
claims.description: The introduction notes the novel's idea of hearing sermons broadcast at home.

claims.quote: Much which is now established in Soviet Russia bears at least a likeness to the industrial army visioned in this prophetic book.
claims.description: The introduction compares Soviet arrangements to the book's national 'industrial army' of conscripted labor.

claims.quote: for he emphasizes repeatedly the non-violent features of the revolution which he imagined
claims.description: The introduction notes the book imagined a non-violent revolution to a cooperative commonwealth.

claims.quote: He sees the change coming through a general recognition of the failings of the capitalist system.
claims.description: The introduction notes the book foresees capitalism replaced through general recognition of its failings.

claims.quote: Indeed, he sees a point in economic development where capitalism may not even be good enough for the capitalist.
claims.description: The introduction notes the book foresees a stage where capitalism fails even the capitalists.

claims.quote: The ingenious device by which a man of the nineteenth century is transferred to the end of the twentieth
claims.description: The sketch describes the novel's device of a nineteenth-century man carried forward to the year 2000.

claims.quote: its definite scheme of industrial organization on a national basis
claims.description: The sketch summarizes the book's plan for all industry organized nationally under the state.

claims.quote: the equal share allotted to all persons in the products of industry, or the public income
claims.description: The sketch summarizes the book's equal share of national output or public income for every person.

claims.quote: the new order which he held that the natural course of social evolution would establish
claims.description: The sketch reports the author's belief that social evolution would naturally bring about the new economic order.

claims.quote: The corner-stone of our state is economic equality
claims.description: Quoted from the sequel: a future state founded on guaranteed economic equality.

claims.quote: how could that be done unless the government conducted the economic system upon which employment and maintenance depend?
claims.description: Quoted from the sequel: the government runs the whole economic system to guarantee everyone work and maintenance.

claims.quote: The great enthusiasm of humanity which overthrew the older and brought in the fraternal society was not primarily or consciously a Godward aspiration at all.
claims.description: Quoted from the novel: a great humane movement overthrows the old order and brings in a fraternal society.

claims.quote: the moment that wall was cast down, the revelation flooded the earth like a sunburst
claims.description: Quoted from the novel: once the inhuman social order falls, a universal religious awakening follows.

claims.quote: Nowadays, as life advances toward its close, instead of being shadowed by gloom, it is marked by an access of impassioned expectancy which would cause the young to envy the old
claims.description: Quoted from the novel: in the future society people face death with joyful expectancy, not dread.

claims.quote: the return of the race by the fulfillment of its evolution, when the divine secret hidden in the germ shall be perfectly unfolded
claims.description: Quoted from the novel: humanity will complete its evolution and fully realize its divine potential.

claims.quote: Living as we do in the closing year of the twentieth century, enjoying the blessings of a social order at once so simple and logical that it seems but the triumph of common sense
claims.description: By the year 2000 a new, simple and logical social order has replaced the nineteenth-century industrial system.
claims.stated_time: the closing year of the twentieth century

claims.quote: How strange and wellnigh incredible does it seem that so prodigious a moral and material transformation as has taken place since then could have been accomplished in so brief an interval?
claims.description: A sweeping moral and material transformation of society is accomplished within less than a century.

claims.quote: These statements seem so absurd on their face, especially when I add that I am a young man apparently of about thirty years of age
claims.description: A man born in 1857 is alive in the year 2000 and still about thirty, having been preserved across more than a century.

claims.quote: This mystery of use without consumption, of warmth without combustion, seems like magic, but was merely an ingenious application of the art now happily lost but carried to great perfection by your ancestors, of shifting the burden of one's support on the shoulders of others.
claims.description: Living on interest and investment income has been abolished and is a lost art by 2000.

claims.quote: Nothing had, however, occurred to modify the immemorial division of society into the four classes, or nations, as they may be more fitly called, since the differences between them were far greater than those between any nations nowadays, of the rich and the poor, the educated and the ignorant.
claims.description: The age-old divisions between rich and poor and between educated and ignorant have disappeared by 2000.
